newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-U.S. analyst Hale says RBA will delay easing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-U.S. analyst Hale says RBA will delay easing.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia is likely to leave any easing of monetary policy until after its December meeting because of concern over recent large pay settlements, influential U.S. economist David Hale said.
"I believe the Reserve Bank will move cautiously because it's still concerned at the lingering inflationary psychology in the corporate sector," Hale told Reuters Financial Television.
Hale, on a visit to Australia as global economist with the Zurich Group, has met in recent days with key policy makers, including Treasury Secretary Ted Evans.
Hale said Australian corporations had suffered a drop in profitability after granting pay increases of five to six percent without corresponding improvements in productivity.
"So if the Reserve Bank eases too quickly, it may cause these corporations to remain complacent and offer wage increases which they simply can't afford," he said.

"It's better then, I think, for the Reserve Bank to move cautiously to remind them that it's not going to return to the kind of wage standard that dominated Australian monetary policy for a generation before."
Data last week showing wage and price inflation at two-year lows had increased expectations that the RBA will decide to cut official interest rates at its monthly meeting on November 5.
However, Hale said he believed the bank would wait until its December meeting before easing so it could see further data on enterprise bargaining agreements in late November.
Hale, who will meet RBA governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday, said he had formed his views from meeting a wide range of contacts in Australia in recent days.
